title: Hourly to Annual Pay: How Salary Sacrifice NSW Affects Your Take-Home Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay with our 38-hour week calculator. Learn how salary sacrifice NSW and state earnings differences impact your income.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: How does salary sacrifice NSW affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice arrangements in NSW allow you to exchange part of your pre-tax salary for benefits like a car or super contributions, reducing your taxable income. Our calculator does not deduct salary sacrifice, so your estimated annual pay is gross before any packaging. For accurate take-home pay after salary sacrifice, consult a tax professional or use the ATO's tools.

faqs.q: What is the difference between NSW and national average weekly earnings?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2026), full-time adult ordinary time earnings in NSW are $2108.80 per week, compared to the national average of $2083.70. This means NSW workers earn about $25.10 more per week on average, which can affect annual pay comparisons.

Yes, superannuation is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. It stops once your earnings reach the $270,830 maximum contribution base. The calculator shows super separately and does not deduct it from your take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Understanding your annual pay from an hourly rate is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee on a standard 38-hour week, the formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice arrangements. It gives you a base figure before tax and super.

### Why 38 Hours?

The Fair Work Ombudsman considers 38 hours the standard full-time week under the National Employment Standards. Many awards and agreements use this as the benchmark. If you work a different number of hours, adjust the formula accordingly. For example, a 40-hour week would use 40 instead of 38.

### The Fortnightly View

Your fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly pay is $2,280. This can help you budget or compare with salary offers quoted per fortnight.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Earnings vary across Australia. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average weekly ordinary time earnings for full-time adults. In May 2026, the national average was $2,083.70 per week. New South Wales (NSW) recorded a higher average of $2,108.80 per week, reflecting the state's strong economy and industry mix.

This difference matters when you're comparing job offers or negotiating pay. A role in NSW might offer a higher hourly rate than the same role in another state, but you should also consider cost of living and other factors.

### How Salary Sacrifice NSW Fits In

Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you give up part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits like a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. In NSW, salary sacrifice is common in both public and private sectors. It reduces your taxable income, which can lower the tax you pay. However, it also reduces your reported gross pay for purposes like loan applications.

Our calculator does not deduct salary sacrifice. The annual pay shown is your gross income before any packaging. If you use salary sacrifice NSW, your actual take-home pay will be different. For a personalised estimate, consider using the ATO's tax withholding tools or speaking with a payroll officer.

## Minimum Wage, Awards, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is set by the Fair Work Commission. Many employees are covered by awards that specify higher minimum rates for their industry or role.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the minimum wage, that's $33.05 per hour. Our calculator has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading. Do **not** type a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator adds it for you.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It does not come out of your hourly rate. The maximum earnings base for super in 2026–27 is $270,830. Our calculator estimates super as 12% of your annual gross, up to that limit.

## Tax and Medicare

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

## Using Our Calculator

To get started, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate. Check the casual loading box if applicable. The calculator will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated super and tax. Remember: this is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed pay guides, see our [pay guides](/blog). You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for award rates and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) by state. If you're interested in salary sacrifice NSW, check our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more information.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
